summary.prose: S003 makes the in-chat permission card settle into a decided state: once the user approves or rejects, the card shows the outcome (green approved / red rejected) and drops its approve/reject buttons, the host records a persisted permission-outcome row so the decision survives reload, and the synthesized 'Approved: please proceed…' grant prompt no longer appears as a fake user line — while the underlying resume turn that actually conveys the grant runs exactly as today. All additive within the one dev-chat render pipeline (P2 over the existing approval-request, instantiated via a P1 persisted row), behind insrc.chat.enabled.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Chosen framework (a1): extend the existing single render pipeline through two HLD-level patterns applied additively, never reshaping a shipped contract. P1 (additive row kind): RowKind + RowViewModel + toViewModel(dual-input live TurnEvent + replayed TranscriptEntry) + markerFor branch + plain-serialisable TranscriptEntry round-tripped by both stores. P2 (live-only interactive prompt -> persisted outcome): a pending request stays markerFor->null (never persisted); the webview relays the decision; on resolution the host records a PERSISTED outcome marker (via P1) showing the decided state WITHOUT altering the underlying action. S003 applies P2 to the EXISTING approval-request event (persisted resolved-outcome marker + suppressed synthesized echo) while leaving the shipped resume-grant untouched (k4).

boundary.internal: The approval-card resolved-state render, the suppressed synthesized grant echo, and the persisted permission-outcome marker; the resume-grant path + permission-decision relay are consumed UNCHANGED (k4).

adjacentBoundaries.internal: input row + width (S002) — out of scope.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: S003 owns sc2 and instantiates it exactly per its interfaceSketch: additive RowKind 'permission-outcome' + PermissionOutcomeRowView + a plain-serialisable TranscriptEntry variant + a toViewModel branch + a markerFor case; the pending approval-request TurnEvent stays markerFor->null (live-only), and the existing permission-decision WebviewToHost message + the shipped resume/grant path are consumed UNCHANGED (k4). The resolved-card DOM state + the runTurn suppress-echo flag realize the 'show the decided state without altering the underlying action' half of the contract.

errorCases.scenario: A permission-decision arrives for a requestId that has no pending entry (already decided, stale, or unknown).
errorCases.detection: The permission-decision handler looks up pendingPerms.get(msg.requestId) and finds undefined (chat-panel.ts:754).
errorCases.response: It falls through to the existing codex/in-turn decide() relay (chat-panel.ts:787-794), which no-ops on an unknown/stale/dead requestId. No permission-outcome entry is recorded for a decision with no matching pending gate.
errorCases.userImpact: A late or duplicate click is a safe no-op; no spurious outcome row and no double grant.

errorCases.scenario: The persisted transcript is loaded from an older (pre-S003) session with no permission-outcome entries.
errorCases.detection: The store's schema validation accepts the union without the new variant (additive/optional); replay encounters no permission-outcome entries.
errorCases.response: toViewModel + the renderer are never invoked for the new kind; the transcript replays exactly as before (no migration needed).
errorCases.userImpact: Older chats load unchanged; no error.

errorCases.scenario: A permission-outcome is recorded but its renderer/toViewModel branch is somehow unmatched (defensive: a malformed decision value).
errorCases.detection: renderRow falls back to the 'fallback' renderer for any kind with no registered renderer (render-registry.ts:90/168); toViewModel's default path handles an unrecognised shape.
errorCases.response: The row renders via the fallback (plain text) rather than throwing; the exhaustive markerFor never-default is preserved by adding the explicit case.
errorCases.userImpact: Worst case a decided outcome shows as a plain line instead of a chip; never a crash or a lost grant.

edgeCases.input: A dir-block permission decision is approved (blockKind === 'dir-block').
edgeCases.expected: The existing informational-message branch (chat-panel.ts:764-775) runs UNCHANGED (no runTurn, no grant); S003 records the permission-outcome (approved) but suppresses no echo there because that branch never posted a user-row echo. The informational assistant message still appears.
No resume turn runs today (deny drops); S003 records a permission-outcome with decision:'rejected' and the card resolves red with buttons removed. No grant, no echo.

edgeCases.input: A tool-gate approve with a concrete command vs the tool-name fallback (chat-panel.ts:779 vs :782).
edgeCases.expected: Both grant re-runs pass { suppressEcho: true } so neither posts a user-row echo, while both still run the resume turn + grant. The recorded outcome is identical (approved).

edgeCases.input: The live approval card is decided, then the session is reloaded.
edgeCases.expected: The pending card (live-only, markerFor->null) does not reappear; the persisted permission-outcome replays as a non-actionable resolved chip (ac4).

edgeCases.input: The same requestId is clicked twice quickly.
edgeCases.expected: pendingPerms.delete on the first decision (chat-panel.ts:756) means the second click finds no pending entry -> the stale-relay no-op path; exactly one outcome recorded, one grant.

invariantsToPreserve.text: The pending approval-request TurnEvent stays LIVE-ONLY: never persisted (markerFor->null default), appended un-keyed (chat-panel.ts:412), so it never enters the durable transcript (k2/ac4).

The shipped Approve grant path is byte-identical: the resume turn (runTurn at chat-panel.ts:779/:782), the pendingPerms correlation, the [toolName] allow, and the permission-decision message are UNCHANGED; only the user-row echo post (chat-panel.ts:543) is gated by the new optional suppressEcho flag (k4/lc1/ac3).
The existing codex/in-turn decide() relay (chat-panel.ts:787-794) and the dir-block informational branch (chat-panel.ts:764-775) are preserved unchanged for requests with no pending tool-gate entry.
The persisted permission-outcome TranscriptEntry is plain-serialisable and round-trips both stores, mirroring S001's tool-result variant.

migration.stateBefore: A pending permission request renders a LIVE-ONLY .insrc-approval card (render-registry.ts:315-330) whose approve/deny buttons post {type:'permission-decision'} (chat-panel.ts:361); the card is appended un-keyed on approval-request (chat-panel.ts:412) and never persists. On Approve of a pending tool-gate the host re-runs via runTurn (chat-panel.ts:779/:782); runTurn posts a VISIBLE user-row echo for EVERY turn (chat-panel.ts:543). So today the card leaves its live buttons after a decision, the decision is not recorded, and the synthesized grant prompt shows as a fake user line.
migration.stateAfter: On approve/deny the live card resolves (approved/rejected class, actions removed, ac1); the host records a plain-serialisable permission-outcome TranscriptEntry (persisted + emitted live) that replays as a non-actionable chip while the pending card never reappears (ac4/k2); the two grant re-runs pass runTurn { suppressEcho: true } so no user-row echo is posted (ac2) while the resume turn + grant run byte-identically (ac3/k4). Additive throughout.

migrationSteps.action: Add the 'permission-outcome' member to RowKind and the PermissionOutcomeRowView payload in render-registry.ts.
Add the plain-serialisable { kind:'permission-outcome'; toolName; decision } variant to the TranscriptEntry union in session-store.ts.
Add the toViewModel branch and register the 'permission-outcome' renderer in both the module copy and the eval'd renderRegistryWebviewSource, keeping the parity test green.
Add the markers.ts markerFor case for the persisted permission-outcome; leave the pending approval-request unmapped (-> null).
Extend the approval renderer's click path to set a resolved class + remove .insrc-approval__actions before/as it calls DEC (ac1).
Add the optional { suppressEcho?: boolean } parameter to runTurn and gate the user-row echo post on it (default off).

In the permission-decision handler, on approve AND deny push the permission-outcome TranscriptEntry (emit live) and pass { suppressEcho: true } to the two grant re-runs. Leave the dir-block + codex relay unchanged.
Add/extend the *WebviewSource + session-store + markers tests per the test strategy.

migration.backwardCompat: runTurn's new third parameter is optional and defaults to today's behaviour, so its existing call-sites + signature stay backward-compatible (k1). The TranscriptEntry, RowKind, and markerFor changes are purely additive: older transcripts replay unchanged (no data rewrite), and consumers ignoring the new kind are unaffected. The approval-request event, permission-decision message, pendingPerms, resume/grant path, dir-block branch, and codex decide() relay are all unchanged, so the shipped Approve behaviour (k4) is preserved — only the visible echo and the added resolved-state/outcome rendering change.

alternativesConsidered.name: P1 persisted permission-outcome row + webview-resolved card + runTurn suppress-echo flag
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add a plain-serialisable 'permission-outcome' row (P1) recorded on decision; mark the live card resolved (green/red, buttons removed); give runTurn an explicit suppress-echo flag the two grant re-runs pass.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Additive P1 (RowKind + view + TranscriptEntry + toViewModel + markerFor) for the persisted outcome; webview-local resolved-card DOM state in the approval renderer's click path; an explicit optional runTurn suppressEcho flag passed only by the two synthesized grant re-runs, so the resume turn + grant run unchanged while the user-row echo is skipped. approval-request event, permission-decision message, and grant path all UNCHANGED.
pros: Meets all four ACs cleanly (ac1 resolved card, ac2 no echo, ac3/k4 grant byte-identical, ac4/k2 pending live-only + persisted outcome replay).
Follows the HLD sc2/P1 pattern verbatim, consistent with S001's shipped tool-result row.
Explicit, intention-revealing echo gate — a normal user turn is never accidentally suppressed.
cons: Largest (but fully additive) surface of the three.
runTurn gains an optional parameter the two grant call-sites pass.

alternativesConsidered.name: Suppress the echo by detecting the synthesized grant prompt text in runTurn
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Same as a1 but suppress the echo by string-matching the known grant phrasings instead of an explicit flag.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Identical persisted-outcome + resolved-card moves; ac2 achieved by testing the prompt text against the two synthesized grant phrasings in runTurn (chat-panel.ts:543) and skipping the user-row post on a match.
pros: Same persisted-outcome + resolved-card behaviour as a1.
cons: Fragile string-coupling: silently breaks if the grant phrasing changes (it lives in a different concern) with no test signal.
False-positive risk: a real user message starting with 'Approved: please proceed…' would be wrongly suppressed — a correctness hazard.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Partial on ac2/k3: string-coupling to the grant phrasings is fragile and risks false-positive suppression of genuine user input — the explicit flag avoids both.

alternativesConsidered.name: Webview-only resolved card; no persisted outcome row
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Mark the card resolved + suppress the echo via the a1 flag, but do NOT persist any outcome.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Do the resolved-card DOM change (ac1) + the runTurn suppress-echo flag (ac2/ac3), but skip the P1 persisted permission-outcome row entirely — the decided state lives only in live DOM.
pros: Satisfies ac1/ac2/ac3 during the live session.
cons: FAILS the intent of ac4/k2: on reload the outcome is LOST — the transcript shows no record of the decision.
VIOLATES sc2, which explicitly requires recording a PERSISTED resolved-outcome marker on decision.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Violates sc2 and only partially meets ac4/k2 — it drops the persisted outcome the HLD contract and the story's user value both require.
